description: Frontend (static/index.html) + README.md: surface the VERIFY tier and DNS reporting added by FEAT-001. Add VERIFY to the risk-badge whitelist (amber/orange, between MEDIUM and HIGH), to the sort order, the risk-breakdown chart/counts, and a Verify filter button; add a DNS column (dns_status) and show the full cname_chain — all XSS-safe (escapeHtml/textContent/safe title, never innerHTML of server data). Document the new VERIFY tier, CLOUD_RESOURCE_PATTERNS coverage, dns_status values, cname_chain, and the 12th CSV column in README. Depends on FEAT-001's results JSON (verify count, dns_status, cname_chain) and the 12-column CSV; implement after FEAT-001.
steps: Read /home/aravind/New-SEC/.agents/tasks/task-takeover-dns/context.json and this FEAT file FIRST. Then read static/index.html (riskBadge, applySort riskOrder, applyFilters, renderTable, displayResults, risk-breakdown bar, summary cards, #filterBtns, escapeHtml/statusCell, results <thead>) and README.md before editing.

In riskBadge: add 'VERIFY' to the whitelist and give it a distinct amber/orange color between MEDIUM and HIGH (e.g. bg-amber-500 text-black), keeping the whitelist + fixed-class approach (no raw interpolation).
In applySort: change riskOrder to { HIGH:4, VERIFY:3, MEDIUM:2, LOW:1, NONE:0 }.
In #filterBtns: add a button data-filter="verify" labeled 'Verify' (styled like the other filter buttons); add case 'verify': return r.takeover_risk === 'VERIFY'; to applyFilters.

Add VERIFY to the risk-breakdown chart: add a #barVerify amber segment and a legend entry; in displayResults compute/display the VERIFY count from data.verify (add a VERIFY summary card or integrate into the breakdown counts), adjusting the 'none' remainder math to subtract verify as well.
Add a 'DNS' column to the results <thead> and render r.dns_status in each row via escapeHtml/textContent (never raw). Keep all existing columns in place.

Render the full cname_chain XSS-safe: either as the CNAME cell full value or as a title on the CNAME cell, joined with ' -> ', escaped with escapeHtml (for a title attribute) / textContent. Keep the existing single-cname display behavior; never innerHTML server data.

Update README.md: document the VERIFY tier (potential dangling cloud resource; manual ownership confirmation required; ordering HIGH > VERIFY > MEDIUM > LOW > NONE), CLOUD_RESOURCE_PATTERNS provider coverage, the dns_status field and its six values (RESOLVED/NXDOMAIN/NO_ANSWER/SERVFAIL/TIMEOUT/ERROR), cname_chain (additive JSON), and the new 12th CSV column; update the CSV-columns block to the 12-column list and the Features bullet that lists risk tiers.
acceptance_criteria: A Node render-helper check (mirroring .agents/tasks/security-audit.md section 11) feeding takeover_risk:'VERIFY' renders an amber VERIFY badge; feeding an XSS payload in dns_status/cname/cname_chain produces escaped, inert output (no raw <script>/on* handlers); riskBadge still maps unknown risk values to NONE.

static/index.html contains a Verify filter button (data-filter="verify"), a 'verify' case in applyFilters, VERIFY in the applySort riskOrder (=3), a VERIFY segment/count in the risk breakdown, and a DNS column showing dns_status.
README.md documents the VERIFY tier, CLOUD_RESOURCE_PATTERNS coverage, dns_status values, cname_chain, and lists 12 CSV columns ending with dns_status.
No regression: .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q still passes (backend untouched by this feature).

findings:
Implemented frontend (static/index.html) + README.md surfacing of the FEAT-001 VERIFY tier and DNS reporting. Verification: render-helper check (.agents/tasks/task-takeover-dns/verify_feat002.js) ALL PASS; .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -> 130 passed (no backend regression); grep confirms VERIFY (7x each) and the 12-column CSV list in README.md + static/index.html.

static/index.html changes (all XSS-safe, no innerHTML of server data):
- riskBadge: added 'VERIFY' to the HIGH|VERIFY|MEDIUM|LOW|NONE whitelist with a fixed amber class (bg-amber-500 text-black, dark text for contrast), sitting between MEDIUM and HIGH; unknown values still collapse to NONE. Kept the fixed-class approach (no raw interpolation).
- applySort riskOrder -> { HIGH:4, VERIFY:3, MEDIUM:2, LOW:1, NONE:0 }.
- applyFilters: added case 'verify' -> r.takeover_risk === 'VERIFY'. New filter button data-filter="verify" labeled 'Verify' between HIGH and MEDIUM, styled like the others.
- Risk breakdown bar: added #barVerify amber segment (ordered HIGH, VERIFY, MEDIUM, NONE) + amber legend entry. displayResults reads data.verify (default 0), sets a new amber #cardVerify summary card, and the 'none' remainder now subtracts verify too (data.total - high - verify - medium). Summary-card grid widened to lg:grid-cols-5.
- Results table: added a sortable 'DNS' column (sorts dns_status) after CNAME, rendering r.dns_status via escapeHtml with an em-dash fallback. cname_chain surfaced as an escapeHtml-ed ' -> '-joined title attribute on the CNAME cell when length>1; the single-cname cell text is unchanged.

README.md changes:
- Features bullet now lists HIGH / VERIFY / MEDIUM / LOW / NONE and mentions dns_status + multi-hop cname_chain.
- New 'Takeover risk tiers' section (HIGH > VERIFY > MEDIUM > LOW > NONE) describing VERIFY as a potential dangling cloud resource requiring manual ownership confirmation, plus a 'Cloud resource coverage (CLOUD_RESOURCE_PATTERNS)' subsection listing AWS ELB/S3/CloudFront, Azure Web Apps/Traffic Manager/Cloud App/Blob, Heroku, GitHub Pages, Google Storage/App Engine, Fastly, noting anchored matching and no-extra-request / SSRF-preserving behavior.
- New 'DNS reporting' section documenting the six dns_status values (RESOLVED/NXDOMAIN/NO_ANSWER/SERVFAIL/TIMEOUT/ERROR), resolved derived strictly as dns_status=='RESOLVED' (CNAME-only -> resolved:false), and the additive cname_chain JSON array (first element == single cname, empty when no CNAME, title in UI).
- CSV report format block updated to the 12-column list ending with dns_status, noting dns_status is appended 12th and the first 11 keep their order.

No backend files (main.py, tests) were modified. All existing columns, filters, and behavior preserved.
